Re:       PUC Docket No. 59475; SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349 – Joint Application of Oncor
          Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Service Corporation to Amend
          Their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity for the Bell County East Switch to Big Hill
          Substation 765-kV Transmission Line Project in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell, Lampasas,
          Llano, Mason, McCulloch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green, and
          Williamson Counties

Dear Mr. Olson,

        On August 20, 2026, the SOAH Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) filed a Proposal for
Decision (PFD) to be considered by the Commissioners. On that same date, Commission Counsel
filed a memorandum in Docket No. 59475 setting the deadline for parties to file exceptions to the
Proposal for Decision on September 2, 2026. The memorandum also set a deadline for filing replies
to exceptions on September 9, 2026.

        On September 2, 2026, several parties filed exceptions to the ALJ’s PFD (Excepting
Parties). The Commission’s procedural rules outline the applicable standard of review that the
Commission must apply in this proceeding.

          Under 16 TAC § 22.262(a):

          [t]he commission may change a finding of fact or conclusion of law made by the
          administrative law judge . . . only if the commission . . . determines that the
          administrative law judge [either] . . . did not properly apply or interpret applicable
          law, commission rules or policies, or prior administrative decisions; or . . . issued a
          finding of fact that is not supported by a preponderance of the evidence . . . or
          determines that . . . a prior administrative decision on which the administrative law
          judge relied is incorrect or should be changed. 1




1     16 TAC § 22.262(a) (emphasis added).
        Applying the standard laid out above, the Commission may modify the PFD, only if the
Excepting Parties establish that the ALJs issued an inadequately supported finding of fact or
erroneously applied PURA § 37.056 and 16 TAC § 25.101. Many of the Excepting Parties have
not made such a showing.

       As such, Theon Ranches, LP, Daniel and Kathryn Voss, (Theon-Voss) and D & M Davis
Land And Cattle, L.P. (D & M Davis) files this letter to continue to express its support for the
Proposal for Decision’s recommendation to deny the application. In the alternative, if the
Commission determines otherwise, Theon-Voss and D&M Davis urge the Commission to select
Route 894.

Respectfully submitted,

/s Alfred R. Herrera
Alfred R. Herrera
State Bar No. 09529600
Herrera Law and Associates
4400 Medical Parkway
Austin, Texas 78756

Attorney for the Theon-Voss and D&M Davis
